needs.triageReason: The solution involves characterising feedstock variance, selecting and validating off-the-shelf pre-conditioning equipment—a materials testing and process integration task, not a research problem.

restatement.text: Suncokret Eko's pellet press line breaks down roughly once a month due to inconsistent feedstock properties from different suppliers. Sunflower husk material arrives with moisture content ranging from 8% to 22% and particle size from fine powder to chunks over 15 mm; moisture above 14% causes die clogging and uneven particle-size distribution leads to bearing failures. The in-line NIR sensor only covers moisture and is unreliable below 10% or above 18%, and there is no automated particle-size check. Each breakdown costs approximately 15,000 EUR in lost production, emergency maintenance and contract penalties. The company has identified secondary hammer mill and conditioning mixer equipment but has not confirmed whether the specified pre-processing equipment would stabilise output enough to prevent failures. The need is a clearer picture of what incoming feedstock variance is acceptable and what pre-processing steps would bring current suppliers' material inside that range (C007-CH3).

proposals.markdown:
## Subsystem Power-Budget Audit and Redesign to Cut KL-Patch 72 Active Current by 35%

**Company:** Kardiolink a.d. works in medtech and digital health. [C005] Challenge C005-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Filip Mijatović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0905]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
The KL-Patch 72 consumes 18 mAh per day when Bluetooth is active and runs on a 54 mAh lithium cell, so active patients who trigger frequent syncs risk battery depletion before the 72-hour wear period ends. [C005-CH1, C005] The company needs to reduce active current draw by at least 35% while maintaining 250 Hz ECG sampling; clinical signal validity depends on holding that sampling floor. [C005-CH1] Kardiolink has already tuned BLE advertising intervals, moved to BLE 5.0 long-range PHY, and switched to a lower-power MCU variant, and is now within a few milliamps of what firmware changes alone can achieve. [C005-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2021 study reports multi-level power optimization of an ambulatory EEG monitoring system on a reconfigurable processor, achieving 73.1% energy reduction over software-only implementation while maintaining real-time seizure detection. [W3206057408]
- A 2022 study reports experimental characterisation of packet forwarding efficiency and duty-cycle configurations for battery-powered BLE relay nodes across multiple scenarios. [W3217361478]

### Research questions
1. Can a redesigned analog front-end and ADC operating point, derived from sub-threshold biopotential circuit techniques, reduce the combined AFE-plus-ADC active current by at least 35% on the KL-Patch 72 reference hardware at 250 Hz, measured with the Keysight N6705C against the current baseline profile?
2. Can event-driven BLE radio scheduling, adapted from wake-up-receiver and duty-cycle MAC principles, cut radio-subsystem current during active wear without dropping a sync cycle, measured as total radio energy per 72-hour session on the reference hardware?
3. Does the combined AFE, ADC, and radio optimisation meet the ≥35% whole-device active-current reduction target while ECG signal quality, assessed against a clinical reference recording at 250 Hz, remains unaffected?

### Approach
- Conduct a full active-current audit using the Keysight N6705C: record per-subsystem current waveforms for the AFE, ADC, BLE radio, and MCU under a standardised 72-hour wear simulation to establish a numbered baseline and identify the dominant consumers.
- Apply sub-threshold and low-quiescent-current biopotential front-end design principles — drawn from published ultra-low-power mixed-signal AFE work — to reconfigure or redesign the analog front-end and ADC operating points on the nRF52840 platform, targeting reduced quiescent current without altering the 250 Hz sampling path.
- Adapt event-driven idle-state management and duty-cycle slot-allocation principles — drawn from wake-up-receiver and MAC scheduling research — to the BLE stack on FreeRTOS, scheduling radio activity around ECG data bursts to reduce radio-on time without missing sync deadlines.
- Validate the combined design on the instrumented reference hardware: measure whole-device active current and record a 250 Hz ECG trace for clinical signal-quality comparison, confirming the ≥35% reduction target is met.

### Plan

| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student, supervised by Filip Mijatović and a company firmware engineer, runs the full subsystem audit on the reference hardware using the Keysight N6705C. They document per-subsystem current waveforms under a standardised 72-hour wear simulation and identify which subsystems account for the largest share of active current. | Numbered baseline current profile per subsystem; ranked list of optimisation targets with estimated headroom, shared with both teams. |
| Months 4–6 | The master's student implements AFE and ADC operating-point changes guided by sub-threshold biopotential front-end principles, and adapts duty-cycle radio scheduling for the BLE stack on FreeRTOS. Each change is tested incrementally on the reference hardware; ECG signal quality is checked at each step against the 250 Hz baseline recording. | Prototype firmware and hardware configuration achieving the target current reduction; measured validation report confirming ≥35% reduction and unaffected 250 Hz ECG quality. |
| Months 7–9 | The team runs a 72-hour endurance test on the optimised device under a realistic sync-load scenario, documents the full design rationale, and prepares a joint technical report. Findings are prepared for submission to an IEEE sensors or biomedical circuits venue. | Final validated design, technical report delivered to Kardiolink, and a joint manuscript submitted for publication. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: Kardiolink provides the master's student with access to the instrumented reference hardware and the Keysight N6705C; both teams agree on the wear-simulation protocol and the current-measurement procedure.
- Month 1: The master's student runs the baseline audit, records per-subsystem current waveforms, and produces the numbered current profile. Filip Mijatović reviews the profile and sets the optimisation priorities.
- Months 2–3: Filip Mijatović identifies AFE and ADC reconfiguration options from sub-threshold front-end design principles; the master's student implements and measures each change on the reference hardware, confirming the 250 Hz sampling floor is held at each step.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Kardiolink provides instrumented reference hardware and a Keysight N6705C power analyzer capable of delivering full active-current profiles across all subsystems. [C005-CH1] The company runs FreeRTOS on an ARM Cortex-M4 with a Nordic Semiconductor nRF52840 handling ECG acquisition at 250 Hz and BLE communication. [C005, C005/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware Engineer — Low-Power BLE Systems] Kardiolink has twelve people across hardware, firmware, and algorithm development with a shared lab equipped for electronics prototyping, signal acquisition testing, and device-level EMC pre-compliance testing. [C005]
- **Faculty:** Filip Mijatović co-authored work on analog front-end circuits for biopotential acquisition achieving sub-microwatt quiescent currents. [SYN-PUB-09637, SYN-PUB-09629] Filip Mijatović co-authored work on wake-up receiver circuits for body-area networks enabling event-driven sensing and idle-state power reduction. [SYN-PUB-07802] Filip Mijatović is open to joint projects with medical device companies and to student internships at M.Sc. level with hardware orientation. [R0905]

### Why this pair
The KL-Patch 72 problem is a subsystem-level power engineering challenge that standard firmware tuning cannot solve; it requires expertise in ultra-low-power analog front-end design and radio duty-cycle scheduling applied to specific measurement hardware. Mijatović brings published methods in sub-microwatt biopotential AFE design and event-driven MAC scheduling that map directly onto the AFE, ADC, and BLE radio subsystems identified in the audit. Neither side could complete this alone: Kardiolink has the instrumented hardware, the BLE platform, and the clinical constraints, while Mijatović brings the circuit and protocol-layer techniques needed to find the remaining headroom those constraints permit.

- The KL-Patch 72 consumes 18 mAh per day on a 54 mAh cell and must cut active current by at least 35% at a fixed 250 Hz floor, after all firmware optimisations are exhausted. [C005-CH1, C005]
- Filip Mijatović co-authored work on analog front-end circuits for biopotential acquisition achieving sub-microwatt quiescent currents and on event-driven wake-up receivers for body-area networks. [SYN-PUB-09637, SYN-PUB-09629, SYN-PUB-07802]

### Risks and constraints
- The published duty-cycle scheduling work covers IEEE 802.15.4; the company's radio stack is BLE on nRF52840. [SYN-PUB-09632, C005]
- The researcher's profile states limited bandwidth until mid-2025. [R0905]
- The compressed-sensing work covers sparse signal reconstruction in wireless body-area networks; C005-CH1 states the 250 Hz sampling rate cannot drop. [SYN-PUB-09636, C005-CH1]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: Kardiolink reviews any manuscript for up to 60 days before submission; either party may request removal of device-specific parameters it considers commercially sensitive.
- Ownership: Kardiolink owns the optimised firmware, hardware configurations, and any design modifications produced in the project; the University of Novi Sad retains the right to use the general methods and findings for teaching and further research.
- Data access: Kardiolink provides the master's student with access to the reference hardware and measurement equipment on-site for the duration of the project; raw current-profile data stays on company premises and is shared with the research team only under a signed NDA.
- Preconditions: The project starts after both parties sign a collaboration agreement covering IP ownership, data confidentiality, and the master's student's affiliation and insurance at the company site.

proposals.title: Synthetic Augmentation and Transfer Learning for Serbian Commercial-Dispute Outcome Prediction
proposals.markdown:
## Synthetic Augmentation and Transfer Learning for Serbian Commercial-Dispute Outcome Prediction

**Company:** PravniPilot a.d. works in legal tech. [C006] Challenge C006-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Jovan Puzović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0484]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
A case-outcome prediction model trained on roughly 9,000 labelled Serbian commercial-dispute decisions achieves 61% accuracy, and the company estimates 40,000 clean labelled decisions are needed to reach accuracy worth advertising. [C006-CH1] Basic data augmentation and fine-tuning of pre-trained multilingual models have not moved accuracy past 63% in internal tests. [C006-CH1] Serbian courts do not publish decisions in a consistent machine-readable format, requiring significant cleaning before any decision can be used for training. [C006-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2023 study reports that multi-language transfer learning with extractive and abstractive techniques outperforms state-of-the-art extractive summarization on a low-resource legal corpus, setting a new baseline for abstractive summarization. [W4387008943]
- A 2023 study reports that a translate-and-test pipeline separating translation from classification significantly improves cross-lingual text classification over competitive multilingual baselines on three benchmark datasets. [W4386902339]

### Research questions
1. Can conditional language-model augmentation and rule-based paraphrasing, applied to the company's ~9,000 labelled decisions, raise outcome-prediction accuracy to 75% on a held-out test set — measured against two independent annotators' consensus labels on at least 1,000 withheld decisions?
2. Does intermediate pretraining on Croatian and Bosnian commercial-dispute decisions before fine-tuning on Serbian decisions improve accuracy beyond what Serbian-only training achieves — measured by macro-F1 on the same held-out set?
3. Does a retrieval-augmented prediction layer, retrieving the five most similar decisions from the full corpus at inference time, further improve accuracy over the augmentation-and-transfer baseline — measured on the same held-out test set?

### Approach
- Audit and stratify the existing ~9,000 labelled decisions by outcome class and court level; establish a fixed train/validation/test split so all subsequent experiments are comparable.
- Apply conditional language-model augmentation and rule-based paraphrasing to the training partition, targeting the under-represented outcome classes, then evaluate each augmentation variant against the validation set using evaluation protocols that incorporate domain expert judgment.
- Run intermediate pretraining on Croatian and Bosnian commercial-dispute decisions drawn from the company's indexed corpus, then fine-tune the resulting model on Serbian decisions; compare macro-F1 against the augmentation-only baseline.
- Add a retrieval-augmented prediction layer that retrieves similar decisions at inference time using dense retrieval; combine retrieved context with the fine-tuned model and evaluate on the held-out test set against the 75% accuracy target; package the final pipeline for direct integration into the production codebase.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from the researcher's group, supported by the company's data engineer, audits the labelled corpus, establishes the fixed train/validation/test split, and reproduces the current 61% baseline. The researcher reviews the audit and agrees the evaluation protocol with the company. | Documented baseline report; agreed evaluation protocol; clean stratified dataset ready for augmentation. |
| Months 4–6 | The master's student implements conditional language-model augmentation and rule-based paraphrasing on the training partition. The company's annotators validate a sample of synthetic decisions using the internal annotation tool. The company's data scientists allocate roughly two days per week to integration testing. | Augmented training set; validation results showing whether augmentation alone crosses 70%; go/no-go decision on transfer learning path. |
| Months 7–9 | The researcher and master's student run intermediate pretraining on Croatian and Bosnian decisions from the company's corpus, then fine-tune on Serbian decisions. A retrieval-augmented prediction layer is built and evaluated against the augmentation-only model. | Transfer-learning model and retrieval-augmented variant; accuracy report against held-out test set; decision on which combination to take to production. |
| Months 10–12 | The company's data scientists integrate the best pipeline into the production codebase. The master's student documents the method; the researcher and company review results for publication. Final evaluation is run on the full held-out test set. | Production-ready pipeline meeting the 75% accuracy target (or a documented gap report); a paper submitted to a venue in legal NLP or applied ML. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: The company exports the ~9,000 labelled decisions to a secure shared environment; the researcher and data engineer agree on the data-sharing protocol and split strategy.
- Week 3–6: The master's student sets up the training and evaluation infrastructure; the current 61% baseline is reproduced and logged so all future experiments are comparable.
- Month 2–3: The master's student and data engineer audit class balance, label quality, and format inconsistencies; the researcher reviews and proposes the augmentation plan.
- Month 4–6: Conditional language-model augmentation and rule-based paraphrasing are implemented on the training partition; a sample of synthetic decisions is validated by the company's annotators using the internal annotation tool.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Roughly 9,000 labelled commercial-dispute decisions and an internal annotation tool, with one full-time data engineer and two part-time annotators available for data quality and labelling. [C006, C006-CH1] A development team that can allocate roughly two days per week to collaborative research, provided research output integrates directly into the production codebase. [C006]
- **Faculty:** Puzović co-authored work on synthetic data generation for legal NLP using conditional language models, rule-based paraphrasing, and evaluation protocols incorporating domain expert judgment. [SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PRJ-0555] Puzović co-authored work on transfer learning and domain adaptation for legal text classification with intermediate pretraining on a combined Croatian–Serbian multilingual legal corpus. [SYN-PUB-05708] Puzović co-authored work on retrieval-augmented generation for legal outcome prediction combining dense retrieval and sequence-to-sequence models. [SYN-PUB-02145] Puzović co-authored work on judicial decision and outcome prediction using recurrent neural networks and sequence modelling on case trajectories. [SYN-PUB-05709]

### Why this pair
Standard multilingual fine-tuning has not moved accuracy past 63%; the remaining gap calls for synthetic augmentation — methods Puzović has published on for legal NLP — and cross-jurisdictional transfer learning, for which Puzović has published work specifically on Croatian–Serbian legal text. Neither could do this alone: the company owns the labelled corpus, the annotation tool, and the multilingual index of two million decisions that makes transfer learning possible, while the researcher brings the augmentation and retrieval-augmented prediction methods that go beyond what the company's internal team has tried.

- PravniPilot's model achieves 61% accuracy; internal fine-tuning experiments have not moved accuracy past 63%, and the company targets 75% accuracy on a held-out test set within 12 months. [C006-CH1]
- Puzović co-authored work on synthetic data generation for legal NLP and on transfer learning with intermediate pretraining on a Croatian–Serbian multilingual legal corpus. [SYN-PUB-05710, SYN-PUB-05711, SYN-PUB-05708]
- The company has processed over two million court decisions and indexes them using PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch. [C006]

### Risks and constraints
- Puzović co-authored a retrieval-augmented generation study on Serbian civil court decisions; the company's target domain is commercial-dispute decisions. [SYN-PUB-02145, C006-CH1]
- The company targets 75% accuracy within 12 months and has two part-time annotators working on labelling (C006-CH1). [C006-CH1]
- R0484 states Puzović is co-supervising two PhD students whose dissertations are expected in 2026–2027, which limits availability for large new commitments until mid-2026 (R0484). [R0484]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be published after a 30-day review by PravniPilot; no decision text or proprietary label may appear in any published work without written consent.
- Ownership: the trained models, augmented dataset, and production pipeline belong to PravniPilot; the researcher retains the right to publish methods and aggregate results.
- Data access: PravniPilot provides the labelled corpus and corpus access under a signed data-use agreement; the master's student works within a secure environment specified by the company.
- Precondition: the project starts only after the data-use agreement is signed and the baseline is independently reproduced on the company's infrastructure.

### Sources

- SYN-PUB-02145: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law (2026)
- SYN-PUB-05708: Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus (2020)
- SYN-PUB-05709: Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models (2021)
- SYN-PUB-05710: A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets (2022)
- SYN-PUB-05711: Conditional GPT-2 Fine-Tuning for Minority-Class Augmentation in a Small Serbian Court Decision Dataset (2023)

proposals.title: Response-Surface Optimisation of Slow Pyrolysis to Reach ≥70% Fixed Carbon Without Sacrificing Yield
proposals.markdown:
## Response-Surface Optimisation of Slow Pyrolysis to Reach ≥70% Fixed Carbon Without Sacrificing Yield

**Company:** Suncokret Eko d.o.o. works in cleantech — biomass and organic waste valorisation. [C007] Challenge C007-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Đorđe Vukelić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry, Faculty of Technology. [R0992]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
The reactor operates at 500–520°C and produces biochar with around 55% fixed carbon and roughly 28% mass yield, but German and Dutch buyers require at least 70% fixed carbon. [C007-CH1] Raising operating temperature to 650°C or above reaches ≥70% fixed carbon but drops mass yield below 20%, making the economics unviable. [C007-CH1] The company has two years of batch logs covering temperature profiles, feedstock moisture, particle size and output quality on the existing slow-pyrolysis reactor. [C007-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2022 study reports slow pyrolysis of corn cob at 600°C with characterised biochar yields and proximate analysis, showing elevated inorganic nutrient content favourable for soil application. [W4302028689]
- A 2025 review reports that lower temperatures and longer residence times enhance biochar yield and carbon content, while higher temperatures favour gas and liquid production. [W4413824496]

### Research questions
1. What combination of temperature (500–650°C), residence time, and particle size achieves ≥70% fixed carbon in sunflower-husk and maize-cob biochar while keeping mass yield at or above 20% on the existing reactor? Measured by proximate analysis of outputs from a response-surface trial set run on the company's reactor, validated against European Biochar Certificate criteria.
2. Do sunflower husks and maize cobs require different process windows, or does a single set of conditions satisfy ≥70% fixed carbon and ≥20% yield for both feedstocks? Measured by comparing RSM model optima and confirmatory batch results for each feedstock against EBC criteria.

### Approach
- Mine the two-year batch logs using TGA-derived isoconversional kinetics of sunflower husks and particle-size decomposition data to shortlist the temperature–residence-time–particle-size combinations most likely to close the fixed-carbon gap without crossing the yield floor.
- Design a Box-Behnken response-surface experiment varying temperature (500–650°C), residence time, and particle size for both feedstocks and run the designed trials on the company's existing reactor, keeping all other equipment unchanged.
- Characterise every trial's biochar by proximate analysis (fixed carbon, volatile matter, ash) and BET surface area in the researcher's laboratory using the TGA-DSC, BET apparatus, FTIR and Raman spectrometers, and evaluate each output against European Biochar Certificate criteria.
- Fit the response-surface models, identify the process window that meets ≥70% fixed carbon and ≥20% yield, and confirm with three production-scale validation batches on the company's reactor.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–2 | Transfer batch logs to the researcher's lab under NDA. Run TGA on representative sunflower husk and maize cob samples from the company to establish isoconversional kinetic baselines. Design the Box-Behnken experiment (~15 runs per feedstock). Vukelić designs the response-surface experiment and supervises day-to-day TGA runs and batch-log analysis; the company's two technically trained staff carry out reactor trials on site. | Shortlist of 8–10 candidate process conditions; TGA kinetic parameters for both feedstocks; agreed trial schedule for months 2–4. |
| Months 2–4 | Company's two technical staff run the designed trials on the existing reactor following researcher-specified protocols. Researcher visits for key trial days. Master's student characterises all outputs in the researcher's lab by proximate analysis, BET, FTIR and Raman. | Full characterisation dataset (~30 trial batches); confirmed fixed-carbon and yield figures for each designed condition. |
| Months 4–5 | Master's student fits RSM models; researcher identifies the optimal process window for each feedstock and checks ANOVA significance. Company staff prepare reactor for validation runs. | RSM models for fixed carbon and yield as functions of temperature, residence time and particle size; recommended operating protocol for each feedstock. |
| Month 6 | Company staff run three confirmatory production batches per feedstock using the recommended protocol. Master's student and researcher compare outputs against model predictions and EBC criteria. Final report and journal paper draft prepared. | Validated operating protocol ready for immediate production use; EBC-ready characterisation data; joint paper draft submitted. |

### First six months
- Weeks 1–2: company provides a representative sample of sunflower husks and maize cobs and transfers two years of batch log files to the researcher under a signed NDA; researcher's master's student sets up a log-analysis spreadsheet and begins TGA runs.
- Weeks 3–6: master's student completes TGA kinetic analysis of both feedstocks in the researcher's lab; researcher uses the results to finalise the Box-Behnken design and agrees a reactor trial schedule with company staff.
- Months 2–4: company staff run ~15 designed trials per feedstock on the existing reactor; master's student travels to the company for at least three trial days and collects samples for lab characterisation back at the faculty.
- Months 4–6: master's student fits RSM models under researcher supervision; company staff run three validation batches per feedstock; researcher and company review results together and sign off on the final operating protocol.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** A slow-pyrolysis reactor operating in batch mode at 400–700°C and two years of batch logs covering temperature profiles, feedstock moisture, particle size and output quality. [C007, C007-CH1] Two technically trained staff who can run controlled production trials and maintain detailed process logs. [C007] Proximate and ultimate analysis capability for biochar including fixed carbon, ash and volatile matter measurement. [C007]
- **Faculty:** Response-surface design and fixed-bed reactor experiments for temperature and residence-time optimisation of biochar yield and structural properties. [SYN-PUB-10356, SYN-PUB-05944] TGA pyrolysis kinetics of sunflower husks using isoconversional methods and thermogravimetric analysis of particle size effects on pyrolysis kinetics. [SYN-PUB-10346, SYN-PUB-10351] Laboratory equipment for biochar characterisation: TGA-DSC coupled analyser, fixed-bed tube furnace reactor (up to 1100°C), BET surface area apparatus, FTIR and Raman spectrometers. [R0992] A granted patent on a process for producing certified-grade biochar from sunflower husk by controlled slow pyrolysis with temperature–residence-time feedback control. [SYN-PAT-033]

### Why this pair
The company owns the reactor, the two-year logs and the exact feedstocks where the problem lives, but cannot close the fixed-carbon/yield gap because the experimental design method and characterisation lab are not available in-house. proposals.title: Detecting Random Guessing in Primary-School Mathematics Game Clickstream Logs
proposals.markdown:
## Detecting Random Guessing in Primary-School Mathematics Game Clickstream Logs

**Company:** Zrenjanin Game Works d.o.o. works in game development. [C002] Challenge C002-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Danilo Mitrović is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences. [R1006]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Approximately 4,200 students' clickstream logs from the 2022–23 and 2023–24 school years record timestamp, question ID, answer chosen, time-on-question, and attempt count for every interaction, but the company has no method to separate guessing from genuine learning in that data. [C002-CH1, C002/job/2024-06-01/Freelance Data Analyst — Learning Outcomes Project (Short-Term Contract)] Teachers report that high in-game scores do not always reflect understanding on paper tests, and the company acknowledges that students who click fast can achieve high scores without understanding the material. [C002-CH1, C002/blog/2024-09-10/What We Learned at the Novi Sad Education Technology Gathering] The company needs a testable method to flag probable guessers before the 2025–26 school year so teachers can intervene early. [C002-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2019 study reports a hierarchical mixture model that jointly identifies random guessing and item-level non-response from response times and answer patterns at the item-by-examinee level. [W2983537616]
- A 2020 study reports that combining response-time thresholds with response behaviours improves detection of rapid disengagement compared to time thresholds alone. [W3029100084]

### Research questions
1. Can session-level features engineered from time-on-question and attempt-count sequences — processed by a hidden Markov model — identify a rapid-guessing latent state that predicts low paper-test scores? Measured as precision and recall of the guesser flag against teacher assessments on a held-out subset of students from the 2023–24 data.
2. Can students be segmented into stable behavioural profiles (e.g., effortful, routine, rapid-guessing) using latent profile analysis on the engineered features, and do profile assignments match teacher-reported understanding? Measured as agreement rate between profile membership and teacher classification on the same held-out subset.
3. Can the detection rules be reduced to a small, interpretable decision table — using at most four feature thresholds — that classroom teachers can apply without statistical tools? Measured by a usability check with two teachers from the Zrenjanin and Subotica schools.

### Approach
- Engineer session-level features from the CSV logs: median and variance of time-on-question per session, first-attempt accuracy rate, ratio of minimum-time responses to total responses, and attempt-count distribution. These map directly onto the time-on-question, answer, and attempt-count fields in the company's data.
- Apply a hidden Markov model to each student's sequence of per-question feature vectors to estimate the probability of being in a rapid-guessing latent state at each question. This follows the researcher's published method for detecting latent states and transitions in longitudinal clickstream sequences.
- Use longitudinal latent profile analysis on session-aggregated features to segment students into behavioural archetypes across the two school years, following the researcher's published approach for tracking profile transitions. Profiles are described in plain language for teachers.
- Distil the HMM and profile outputs into an explainable decision table — threshold rules on two to four features — validated against teacher assessments. The table is the deliverable teachers use; the models are the derivation tool.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student, supervised by Mitrović and the company's lead developer (one day per week), transfers and audits the CSV logs, resolves missing values, and engineers the session-level feature set. Mitrović reviews feature definitions against the HMM and latent profile analysis requirements. | A clean, documented feature dataset covering all 4,200 students across both school years; a data-quality report shared with both sides. |
| Months 4–6 | The master's student fits the hidden Markov model and the latent profile analysis on the 2022–23 data. Mitrović supervises model selection and interprets latent states. The company's pedagogy contact reviews whether identified profiles match known student types. The model is validated on the 2023–24 held-out data. | A validated guesser-flag method with precision and recall figures; an interpretable decision table of at most four threshold rules; a draft technical report. Usability check with two teachers from Zrenjanin and Subotica schools. |

### First six months
- Month 1: the company exports the full CSV logs from MySQL and shares them with the research team under a signed data-sharing agreement; the master's student sets up the analysis environment and runs an initial data-quality audit.
- Month 2: the master's student and Mitrović define the feature set (time-on-question statistics, first-attempt accuracy, minimum-time-response ratio, attempt-count distribution) and compute it for all students; the company's lead developer confirms the feature definitions match the log schema.
- Month 3: Mitrović and the master's student fit a baseline threshold classifier (response-time cutoff only, following the published rapid-disengagement literature) to give a reference point for the HMM and latent profile analysis results.
- Months 4–6: fit, validate, and interpret the HMM and latent profile models; produce the decision table; run the teacher usability check with support from the company's pedagogy contact.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Approximately 4,200 students' clickstream logs in CSV from MySQL, covering two school years, with time-on-question, answer, attempt count, and timestamp per interaction. [C002-CH1, C002/job/2024-06-01/Freelance Data Analyst — Learning Outcomes Project (Short-Term Contract)] Mathematics game content for grades one through four deployed in live school environments in Zrenjanin and Subotica, providing the educational context for interpreting model outputs. [C002, C002/website/2024-02-10/What We Do — Zrenjanin Game Works, C002/news/2024-04-22/New Contract: Subotica District Education Office Joins for 2024–25 School Year] The lead developer available approximately one day per week for data access, schema clarification, and integration work, and the pedagogy contact available on a similar basis for teacher liaison. [C002]
- **Faculty:** Mitrović has published on hidden Markov models for detecting latent states and transitions in longitudinal behavioural clickstream sequences. [SYN-PUB-10456] Mitrović has published on longitudinal latent profile analysis to segment students into behavioural archetypes and track profile transitions. [SYN-PUB-10459] Mitrović has published on clickstream feature engineering from learning management system logs using session-aggregated and click-level activity patterns. [SYN-PUB-10457, SYN-PUB-10455] Mitrović completed a four-month consultancy engagement with an e-learning content provider on learner progress scoring system design. [R1006]

### Why this pair
The company has two years of fine-grained interaction logs and direct access to teachers who can validate flags, but no method to extract guessing signals from those logs and no in-house expertise to build one. Mitrović brings the specific methods the problem requires — hidden Markov models for latent behavioural states and latent profile analysis for student segmentation — applied to clickstream data. Neither could do it alone; Mitrović brings the modelling methods and a master's student to do the day-to-day analysis work within the researcher's reduced-capacity window.

- The company has clickstream logs for approximately 4,200 students with time-on-question, attempt count, and answer fields covering two school years. [C002-CH1, C002/job/2024-06-01/Freelance Data Analyst — Learning Outcomes Project (Short-Term Contract)]
- Mitrović has published on hidden Markov models for latent state detection in clickstream sequences and on latent profile analysis for student segmentation. [SYN-PUB-10456, SYN-PUB-10459]
- A teacher from the company's users and teachers encountered at an external education technology gathering have reported that high in-game scores do not always reflect understanding on paper tests. [C002-CH1, C002/blog/2024-09-10/What We Learned at the Novi Sad Education Technology Gathering]

### Risks and constraints
- Mitrović's profile states a reduced teaching load in 2025–2026 due to CROSSLEARN project obligations and limited capacity for additional large commitments before mid-2026. [R1006]
- The published records cover clickstream sequence analysis, aggregated behavioural feature engineering, and segmentation into disengaged, routine, and intensive study states; none covers explicit guessing-parameter modelling or detection of non-effortful responders. [SYN-PUB-10457, SYN-PUB-10459, SYN-PUB-10456, SYN-PUB-10455]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be published after a 30-day review by the company; the company may request redaction of commercially sensitive product details but may not block publication of the method or aggregate findings.
- Ownership: the company owns the trained model parameters, the decision table, and any code integrated into the game platform; the researcher's group retains the general methods and may reuse them in future research.
- Data access: the company provides anonymised student logs to the research team under a signed data-sharing agreement compliant with GDPR and the Serbian Personal Data Protection Law; no individual student may be identified in any publication.
- Preconditions: the data-sharing agreement and ethics approval from the Faculty of Sciences must be in place before any logs are transferred; the project starts only after both are signed.

### Sources

- C002-CH1: Teachers tell us our math games are fun but they can't see whether a child is actually learning — we have clickstream...

- C002/news/2024-04-22/New Contract: Subotica District Education Office Joins for 2024–25 School Year: New Contract: Subotica District Education Office Joins for 2024–25 School Year
- C002/website/2024-02-10/What We Do — Zrenjanin Game Works: What We Do — Zrenjanin Game Works
- R1006: Danilo Mitrović
- SYN-PUB-10455: Temporal Patterns in Student Engagement: A Sequence Clustering Approach (2015)
- SYN-PUB-10456: Applying Hidden Markov Models to Detect Shifts in Student Learning States from Clickstream Data (2017)
- SYN-PUB-10457: Cross-Course Generalisation of Clickstream-Based Performance Predictors: An Empirical Evaluation (2020)
- SYN-PUB-10459: Longitudinal Latent Profile Analysis of Learning Behaviours Across a Three-Year Study Programme (2023)
- W2983537616: A hierarchical latent response model for inferences about examinee engagement in terms of guessing and item‐level non... (2019) https://openalex.org/W2983537616
- W3029100084: Enhancing response time thresholds with response behaviors for detecting disengaged examinees (2020) https://openalex.org/W3029100084

proposals.title: Low-Temperature Thermo-Mechanical Fatigue Analysis of Weld Cracking in Chilled Conveyor Frames
proposals.markdown:
## Low-Temperature Thermo-Mechanical Fatigue Analysis of Weld Cracking in Chilled Conveyor Frames

**Company:** AutomVoj a.d. works in robotics and industrial automation. [C003] Challenge C003-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Bojan Erić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0365]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Welded mild steel conveyor frames are cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after approximately 18 months of chilled operation at 2–6 °C, but the same frames pass load testing at room temperature in the workshop. [C003-CH1] AutomVoj has replaced 14 frame assemblies under warranty this year; two failed sections remain in storage with site-visit photos and measurements. [C003-CH1] The company suspects thermal cycling, condensation, and vibration are interacting to cause the failure, but cannot reproduce or characterise the phenomenon at ambient workshop conditions. [C003-CH1] The workshop does not have equipment or know-how for low-temperature cyclic load testing. [C003-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2023 study reports that welding residual stress significantly increases the effective crack driving force and reduces fatigue life, with the fatigue life at the weld toe without considering residual stress being approximately twice that when residual stress is considered. [W4388490665]

### Research questions
1. Can thermo-mechanical cycling at 2–6 °C under representative conveyor vibration loads reproduce the observed weld-toe cracking mode in laboratory specimens cut from MIG/MAG welded mild steel hollow sections? Measured by crack location, morphology, and depth against fractographic evidence from the two failed field sections.
2. Do welding residual stresses at the crossmember-to-stringer joint, measured by X-ray diffraction on the failed sections and on fresh specimens, reach levels that — combined with service loads — exceed the fatigue crack growth threshold at 2–6 °C? Measured by comparing effective stress intensity factor ranges to the material's low-temperature threshold from Charpy and CTOD tests.
3. Which single mechanism or combination — thermal fatigue, residual-stress-assisted crack growth, or corrosion-fatigue from condensation — governs failure life? Measured by rank-ordering predicted crack growth lives from each mechanism model against the observed 18-month field life.

### Approach
- Cut representative weld specimens from the two failed sections and from fresh MIG/MAG welded hollow-section joints fabricated to AutomVoj's procedure. Perform fractographic examination and hardness mapping to characterise crack initiation sites and heat-affected zone microstructure.
- Measure residual stresses on the failed and fresh specimens by X-ray diffraction, following the method Erić co-authored for weld residual stress measurement. Build a finite element model to compute stress intensity factor ranges at the weld toe under combined residual stress and service loading, using the sequentially coupled thermal–structural and Chaboche cyclic-plasticity modelling approaches from Erić's co-authored FE work on residual stress in welds.
- Apply thermo-mechanical fatigue cycling in the climate chamber at 2–6 °C with superimposed cyclic mechanical loads representative of conveyor vibration, monitoring crack closure and crack opening displacement by digital image correlation, following the method co-authored for combined thermal and mechanical cycling.
- Assess low-temperature fracture toughness of the weld heat-affected zone by Charpy impact and CTOD testing at 2–6 °C following the method co-authored for HAZ microstructures down to −60 °C. Combine all results into a failure characterisation report that identifies the governing mechanism and specifies the weld geometry or procedure change needed to prevent recurrence.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | Transfer both failed sections to the lab. A master's student, supervised by Erić, cuts specimens, performs fractography, hardness mapping, and XRD residual stress measurements. The company engineer provides site-visit records and fabrication procedure documents. | Residual stress map of the failed joint, fractographic failure characterisation report, and identification of crack initiation site. |
| Months 4–6 | Fabricate fresh weld specimens to AutomVoj's MIG/MAG procedure. Run thermo-mechanical fatigue tests in the climate chamber at 2–6 °C with DIC crack closure monitoring. Run Charpy and CTOD tests at 2–6 °C on HAZ specimens. | Reproduced cracking in laboratory specimens; low-temperature toughness data for the joint's HAZ; go/no-go on each proposed failure mechanism. |
| Months 7–9 | Build and validate the FE model of the joint with measured residual stresses. Compute effective stress intensity factor ranges for each mechanism. Rank mechanisms by predicted crack growth life versus observed 18-month field life. | Validated FE model; ranked mechanism assessment; draft fitness-for-service report. |
| Months 10–12 | Define and test at least one revised weld geometry or procedure (e.g., changed toe profile or post-weld treatment) under the same thermo-mechanical cycling protocol. Deliver the final failure characterisation report and design recommendation to AutomVoj. | Final report with identified governing mechanism, tested design or welding change, and recommended specification update for future frames. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: AutomVoj transfers the two failed sections and all site-visit photos, load records, and fabrication procedure documents to the Faculty lab. The company engineer briefs Erić's group on the conveyor duty cycle and operating environment.
- Month 1: The master's student cuts weld-toe specimens from the failed sections. Erić's group performs optical and SEM fractography, Vickers hardness mapping across the HAZ, and XRD residual stress measurements on the failed joint faces.
- Month 2–3: Erić's group fabricates fresh MIG/MAG welded hollow-section specimens to AutomVoj's welding procedure. XRD measurements are taken on the fresh specimens to establish the as-welded residual stress baseline for comparison with the failed sections.
- Month 3–4: First thermo-mechanical fatigue tests run in the climate chamber at 2–6 °C; DIC is set up on the specimen surface at the weld toe. The company engineer reviews interim fractographic findings and confirms whether observed crack locations match those seen on the field failures.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Two failed frame assemblies in storage, with site-visit photos and field measurements, available as primary specimens for analysis. [C003-CH1] An engineering team of 212 engineers, electricians, and technicians available to support the project. [C003] Fabrication shop, electrical assembly area, and in-house testing floor all under one roof on the Zrenjanin site. [C003]
- **Faculty:** Erić co-authored work on fracture toughness of weld HAZ microstructures at temperatures down to −60 °C using Charpy impact and CTOD testing. [SYN-PUB-04476] Erić co-authored work on thermo-mechanical fatigue testing and crack closure measurement by digital image correlation under combined mechanical and thermal cycling. [SYN-PUB-04482, SYN-PUB-04475] Erić co-authored work on residual stress measurement by X-ray diffraction and FE modelling of residual stress relaxation under cyclic loading in S355 cruciform welded joints, and separately on FE simulation of thermal gradient-induced residual stress in welded box sections. [SYN-PUB-04478, SYN-PUB-04481] Erić offers access to a servo-hydraulic fatigue machine, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and a digital image correlation setup. [R0365]

### Why this pair
AutomVoj has the only primary evidence that matters — the two failed sections, the field records, and the exact fabrication procedure — but cannot generate the low-temperature cyclic loading needed to understand or reproduce the failure. Erić's group has the climate chamber, the servo-hydraulic rig, the DIC system, and published methods covering every step of the proposed investigation: low-temperature HAZ toughness, thermo-mechanical fatigue with DIC, and residual stress measurement with FE simulation. Neither side can do this alone: the company has the physical evidence and the production context; the researcher has the equipment and the tested methods to turn that evidence into a governed failure explanation and a prevention recommendation.

- AutomVoj cannot reproduce the failure at ambient conditions and has no equipment for low-temperature cyclic testing, while two failed sections with site records are in storage and ready for analysis. [C003-CH1]
- Erić co-authored publications covering low-temperature fracture toughness of weld HAZ microstructures down to −60 °C and thermo-mechanical fatigue with DIC crack monitoring. [SYN-PUB-04476, SYN-PUB-04482, SYN-PUB-04475]
- Erić offers the servo-hydraulic fatigue machine, climate chamber to −60 °C, and DIC setup that the company's workshop does not have. [R0365, C003-CH1]

### Risks and constraints
- The publications cover structural steels and welds in general; it is not confirmed that the record covers MIG/MAG welded mild steel hollow sections specifically as used in C003 conveyor frames. [SYN-PUB-04476, SYN-PUB-04480, C003]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be submitted for publication after a 60-day written review by AutomVoj; the company may request a further 30-day delay to file for IP protection before submission.
- Ownership: AutomVoj owns the failure characterisation report, the design recommendation, and any revised welding specification; the Faculty retains the right to use the experimental methods and anonymised test data in future research and teaching.
- Data access: AutomVoj provides the failed sections, all site-visit records, fabrication drawings, and welding parameters to the Faculty at project start; the Faculty stores physical specimens securely and returns or destroys them at project end as AutomVoj directs.
- Preconditions: the project starts only after both parties sign a confidentiality agreement covering AutomVoj's fabrication procedures and field incident records; fresh weld specimens are produced by AutomVoj to the production welding procedure before Month 2 testing begins.

### Sources
- C003: AutomVoj a.d.
- C003-CH1: Our conveyor frames crack at the weld joints after roughly 18 months of operation in chilled environments; we've repl...
- R0365: Bojan Erić
- SYN-PUB-04475: Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates (2016)

proposals.title: Unsupervised On-Device Anomaly Detection for Site-Specific Modbus and BACnet Traffic
proposals.markdown:
## Unsupervised On-Device Anomaly Detection for Site-Specific Modbus and BACnet Traffic

**Company:** ArmaturaSec d.o.o. works in cybersecurity. [C001] Challenge C001-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Krisztina Kiss is a Full Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R1008]  
**Format:** industrial PhD, three years. The researcher is the academic supervisor; the company names an industrial supervisor and employs the candidate.

### The problem
ProtoSense is supposed to flag anomalous behaviour, but supervised classifiers trained on public ICS datasets produced unacceptable false positive rates in real deployments, leaving the detection problem unsolved. [C001-CH1, C001/blog/2024-05-20/Why We Stopped Trying to Use Public ICS Datasets for Anomaly Detection] ArmaturaSec has several terabytes of normal Modbus and BACnet traffic from consenting clients over three years but no confirmed malicious examples, making supervised labelling impossible. [C001-CH1] Any anomaly flag must be explained to plant managers in plain language; opaque scores are not acceptable. [C001-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2018 study reports that a deep CNN trained only on unlabelled time-series data can detect point anomalies, contextual anomalies, and discords without requiring labelled attack examples. [W2906498146]

### Research questions
1. Can a one-class detector trained solely on site-captured Modbus and BACnet traffic, using byte-level payload features, achieve a false positive rate below the threshold observed with public-dataset-trained classifiers, measured on ArmaturaSec's multi-site traffic corpus with operator-verified normal labels?
2. Can a quantised and structurally pruned version of the detector run on the fifth hardware variant's security processor without increasing packet forwarding latency, measured by latency benchmarks on the target board under full forwarding load?
3. Does incremental online learning with Bayesian updates keep the detector's false positive rate stable when site-normal behaviour shifts, measured by monitoring flag rates before and after five controlled configuration changes injected into the lab testbed traffic?

### Approach
- Characterise Modbus and BACnet traffic in ArmaturaSec's corpus using byte-level payload feature extraction and periodicity analysis, extending the protocol-agnostic feature pipeline from the researcher's one-class classification work to cover BACnet function codes and timing patterns not previously studied.
- Train and evaluate one-class detectors — including autoencoder ensembles and one-class SVMs — on site-specific captures, using threshold calibration on unlabelled operational data with beta mixture models so that no labelled attacks are needed at any stage.
- Compress the best-performing detector via quantisation and structured pruning of its autoencoder, targeting deployment on the fifth hardware variant's security processor, and benchmark latency under forwarding load to confirm the hard constraint is met.
- Add incremental online learning with Gaussian mixture models and Bayesian updates so that the deployed model adapts when a plant's normal polling rhythm changes, and pair each flag with a plain-language explanation derived from the feature dimension responsible for the highest reconstruction error.

### Plan

| Year | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Year 1 | The candidate, supervised by the researcher and the company engineer, ingests and parses ArmaturaSec's Modbus and BACnet corpus. BACnet protocol behaviour is characterised from scratch using byte-level feature extraction. A labelled-normal reference set is agreed with operators at three client sites. Baseline one-class detectors are trained and evaluated on Modbus traffic first, then extended to BACnet. | A curated multi-site traffic dataset with operator-verified normal labels; a dataset paper; baseline false positive and detection rates on both protocols. |
| Year 2 | The candidate applies threshold calibration using unlabelled operational data and beta mixture models to set per-site thresholds without attack labels. The best model is compressed via quantisation and structured pruning and ported to the fifth hardware variant's security processor. Forwarding latency is benchmarked under load. | An on-device detector prototype running on the target hardware with confirmed latency compliance; a paper on calibration and compression results. |
| Year 3 | The candidate integrates incremental online learning with Gaussian mixture models and Bayesian updates into the on-device model. The plain-language explanation layer is built and evaluated with plant managers at two client sites. A live trial runs for at least three months across water treatment, substation, and manufacturing sites. | A production-ready detector with drift adaptation and plain-language explanations; a final paper; a trial report presented to ArmaturaSec for integration decision. |

### First six months
- Month 1–2: The company engineer transfers a representative sample of Modbus and BACnet captures to the researcher's testbed under a data-sharing agreement. The candidate sets up the ingestion and feature-extraction pipeline and documents BACnet function code distribution across site types.
- Month 2–3: The researcher and candidate review operator logs at two client sites to agree on what counts as normal; these become the reference labels for all evaluation. The company engineer provides site context.
- Month 3–5: The candidate trains initial one-class detectors on Modbus traffic from two sites and measures false positive rates against the reference labels, establishing the baseline the rest of the PhD improves on.
- Month 5–6: The candidate runs the same pipeline on BACnet captures and reports where BACnet behaviour differs from Modbus in ways that affect feature choice, producing a short technical note that guides Year 1 dataset work.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Several terabytes of normal Modbus and BACnet traffic captures collected over three years from consenting clients. [C001-CH1] A bench with physical boards, PLC simulators, and packet generators for controlled traffic experiments and hardware porting. [C001/job/2024-02-05/Firmware Engineer — Network Protocols (Zrenjanin)] One engineer who has been reading about anomaly detection for six months. [C001-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Krisztina Kiss co-authored a protocol-agnostic anomaly detection method for ICS using byte-level payload features and one-class SVM that requires no labelled attack data. [SYN-PUB-10483] Krisztina Kiss co-authored lightweight model compression for embedded ICS gateways through quantisation and structured pruning of autoencoder-based detectors. [SYN-PUB-10239] Krisztina Kiss co-authored incremental online learning with Gaussian mixture models and Bayesian updates for concept drift adaptation, and threshold calibration for anomaly detectors using unlabelled operational data and beta mixture models. [SYN-PUB-00492, SYN-PUB-10480] Krisztina Kiss operates a dedicated ICS testbed with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure available to industrial partners under data-sharing agreements. [R1008]

### Why this pair
The company holds a rare, large corpus of real operational traffic but hit a research-grade obstacle — unsupervised site-specific baseline modelling — that its engineer cannot resolve alone from background reading. The researcher brings the exact combination of methods the problem demands: one-class detection without labels, compression for constrained hardware, and drift-adaptive online learning, all demonstrated on ICS traffic. Neither could do it alone: ArmaturaSec brings several terabytes of site-specific Modbus and BACnet traffic from consenting clients, a bench with physical boards and PLC simulators, and an engineer who has been reading about anomaly detection for six months; the researcher brings the methods, the ICS testbed for controlled experiments, and the supervision to turn three years of work into a deployable system.

- ArmaturaSec has several terabytes of site-specific Modbus and BACnet traffic with no labelled attack examples, requiring an unsupervised approach the company cannot implement from its current reading. [C001-CH1]
- Krisztina Kiss co-authored one-class ICS anomaly detection using byte-level payload features requiring no labelled attacks, compression for embedded ICS gateways, and drift-adaptive online learning for continuous ICS streams. [SYN-PUB-10483, SYN-PUB-10239, SYN-PUB-00492, SYN-PUB-10480]
- Krisztina Kiss is open to supervising industrial PhDs for candidates from companies in automation and critical infrastructure. [R1008]

### Risks and constraints
- The published record covers Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP traffic characterisation and detection; BACnet-specific protocol behaviour is not covered in the cited works (SYN-PUB-10474, SYN-PUB-10473, SYN-PUB-10482). [SYN-PUB-10474, SYN-PUB-10473, SYN-PUB-10482]
- The challenge requires that anomaly flags be explainable to plant managers in plain language (C001-CH1). [C001-CH1]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: ArmaturaSec has 60 days to review any manuscript before submission; ArmaturaSec may request removal of traffic samples or site-identifying details but may not block publication of methods or aggregate results.
- Ownership: ArmaturaSec owns the trained models, the compressed on-device artefact, and all code written for deployment; the University retains the methods, algorithms, and the right to use anonymised results in teaching and future research.
- Data access: ArmaturaSec transfers traffic captures to the researcher's testbed under a written data-sharing agreement specifying that data are used only for this project, stored on access-controlled infrastructure, and deleted or returned at project end.
- Preconditions: The project starts only after the data-sharing agreement is signed, client consent for research use of captures is confirmed in writing, and the candidate's employment contract with ArmaturaSec is in place.

needsHuman.title: Link-Budget Recovery for LoRaWAN Meters in Reinforced-Concrete Basements
needsHuman.markdown:
## Link-Budget Recovery for LoRaWAN Meters in Reinforced-Concrete Basements

**Company:** Elekron Sistemi a.d. works in ioT and electronics hardware. [C008] Challenge C008-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Tihomir Urošević is a Research Associate in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0800]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
LoRaWAN collar devices on water and heat meters in basement meter rooms at three municipal clients receive at -120 to -125 dBm, at gateway sensitivity, losing approximately 9% of daily readings even at SF12. [C008-CH1] The company has been in SLA breach with penalty clauses threatened for six months, and fixed-price municipal contracts bar replacing gateways or re-running cables. [C008-CH1] Repositioning gateway antennas and adding a repeater node brought limited improvement; the ReachRate applied research project must deliver a solution within 14 months. [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research] A Vojvodina Development Fund grant of 4.2 million dinars covers approximately 55% of projected project costs. [C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]

### Prior work
- A 2025 study reports that the number and material composition of obstacles, together with spreading factor and transmit power settings, measurably shift RSSI and SNR in real indoor LoRa deployments. [W4416363698]
- A 2019 study reports that LoRa energy consumption in multifloor buildings varies up to 145 times across parameter settings, and that adaptive data rate selection is important for energy-limited indoor applications. [W2979511419]

### Research questions
1. What is the per-wall and per-floor penetration loss profile in the target basement rooms at 868 MHz, and which propagation mechanism (material loss, multipath, diffraction) accounts for the observed 9% packet drop — measured by a channel-sounding campaign across the three municipal sites and compared against a calibrated path-loss model?
2. Can a compact 868 MHz antenna modification on the collar device, optimised for near-surface mounting in a metal meter enclosure, recover enough link margin to bring missed reads below 1% without changing the gateway or running new cable — measured by field packet-delivery trials at all three sites under normal operating conditions and within LoRaWAN duty-cycle and Class A/C constraints?

### Approach
- Conduct a channel-sounding campaign in the basement meter rooms using vector network analyser and software-defined radio equipment to measure path loss, delay spread, and wall-penetration loss at 868 MHz, applying the empirical and deterministic methods used in the researcher's indoor and material-penetration propagation work.
- Build a per-site link-budget model, calibrated against the measured data, to identify which loss contributions account for the margin shortfall and to bound how much gain a device-side antenna change can recover — following the link-budget prediction approach from the researcher's LoRaWAN planning work.
- Design and prototype one or two compact 868 MHz antenna variants (drawing on the researcher's planar inverted-F antenna work for LoRa) optimised for the constrained geometry of the collar device mounted on a metal meter housing in a low-ceiling reinforced concrete room.
- Run field packet-delivery trials at all three municipal sites with the prototype antenna — logging packet delivery ratio, RSSI, and SNR over at least two full billing cycles — with all LoRaWAN parameters held within duty-cycle limits and Class A/C constraints, to measure whether missed reads fall below 1%.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from the researcher's group, supervised by the researcher and the company's senior RF engineer, deploys channel-sounding equipment across the three municipal basement sites. The company's engineer arranges site access and provides existing RSSI logs. Measurements cover wall thickness, floor penetration, and multipath profile at 868 MHz. | A calibrated per-site path-loss dataset and a written diagnosis identifying which loss mechanism drives the 9% packet drop at each site. |
| Months 4–7 | The master's student builds and calibrates a link-budget model for each site using the measured data. The researcher designs one or two compact 868 MHz antenna variants for the collar form factor, prototyped and characterised in the faculty's reverberation chamber for radiation efficiency. The company's engineer integrates prototypes with production collar firmware. | A link-budget model per site, two antenna prototypes with measured efficiency figures, and a written antenna integration report. |
| Months 8–12 | Field packet-delivery trials run at all three sites using the prototype antenna, with LoRaWAN parameters fixed within duty-cycle limits and Class A/C constraints. The master's student and company engineer jointly log PDR, RSSI, and SNR over at least two billing cycles. Results are compared against the 1% missed-read target. | Field trial report with per-site PDR statistics; a go/no-go decision on each antenna variant; a journal paper co-authored by the researcher and the company engineer. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: In month 1, the researcher's group visits the worst-performing meter room at one municipal site with the SDR channel sounder and vector network analyser to collect baseline RSSI and path-loss measurements; the company's RF engineer attends to provide site access and device configuration.
- Month 1: The company's senior RF engineer arranges site access at the first municipal location; the master's student sets up the channel-sounding rig (vector network analyser and SDR sounder from the faculty lab) and takes baseline wall-penetration and path-loss measurements.
- Months 2–3: Measurement campaign completes across all three sites; the master's student processes data into per-site path-loss and delay-spread profiles; the researcher reviews and calibrates the model against the existing RSSI logs.
- Month 3: The researcher and company engineer hold a joint review meeting to confirm the dominant loss mechanism at each site and agree the antenna design brief (form factor, gain target, mounting constraints) for the collar prototype work in months 4–7.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Three live municipal utility deployments in Bosnia and North Macedonia with real basement meter rooms are available for field testing. [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research] A senior RF engineer who led the original LoRaWAN collar development serves as project lead for ReachRate. [C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research] Access to oscilloscopes, protocol analysers, and environmental test chambers in a small lab in Subotica for device-level testing. [C008] A Vojvodina Development Fund grant of 4.2 million dinars covering approximately 55% of projected project costs. [C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]
- **Faculty:** Urošević co-authored work on a link-budget tool for LoRaWAN deployments using empirical measurement data. [SYN-PUB-08743] Urošević co-authored work on compact planar inverted-F antenna design for 868 MHz LoRa integration. [SYN-PUB-08741] Urošević has access to a reverberation chamber, vector network analyser, and software-defined radio channel sounder for antenna characterisation and propagation measurement campaigns. [R0800] Urošević led a work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation in AGRILINK, a LoRaWAN project with agricultural and university partners. [SYN-PRJ-0350]

### Why this pair
The company has a live, penalty-bearing signal problem in a specific physical environment where repositioning gateway antennas and adding a repeater node brought only limited improvement; Urošević brings propagation measurement equipment and antenna design methods the plan requires. Urošević brings indoor path-loss measurement methods, sub-GHz antenna design for LoRa collar form factors, and prior LoRaWAN link-budget validation on a live project; the company brings the production meter rooms and an active municipal utility network where results can be validated. Together, they can run a targeted measurement-to-prototype cycle that neither could complete alone within 14 months.

- The company's collar devices receive at -120 to -125 dBm in basement meter rooms, losing approximately 9% of daily readings at SF12; fixed-price municipal contracts mean the company does not have budget for a full gateway infrastructure overhaul. [C008-CH1]
- Urošević co-authored work on a link-budget tool for LoRaWAN deployments and on compact planar inverted-F antenna design for 868 MHz LoRa integration. [SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-08741]
- Urošević has access to a reverberation chamber, vector network analyser, and SDR channel sounder, and carried out a paid LoRaWAN coverage measurement study for a logistics company. [R0800]

### Risks and constraints
- The propagation-through-materials work covers greenhouse structures and hospital buildings. [SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08744]
- The ReachRate project must deliver improvements within 14 months, and the fixed-price municipal contracts limit budget for gateway infrastructure overhaul (C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research). [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: the company has 60 days to review any manuscript before submission; results may be published after that window with no redaction of field trial data, provided individual meter-room addresses are anonymised.
- Ownership: the company owns the calibrated site models, the antenna design files, and any trained firmware parameters; the faculty retains the measurement methods and may reuse them in future research.
- Data access: the company provides six months of existing RSSI and PDR logs at project start under a signed data-use agreement; field access to municipal sites is arranged by the company's engineer for each measurement visit.
- Preconditions: the project starts only after the data-use agreement is signed by both parties and site-access approval is confirmed in writing by all three municipal clients.
